'''Jinchōkan Moriya Shiryōkan''' (神長官守矢史料館) is a [[Museum|museum]] located in [[Miyakawa (Chino City)|Miyagawa]], [[Chino, Nagano|Chino City]], [[Nagano Prefecture]], Japan. The museum preserves and displays documents related to the Moriya family, which served as [[Kancho]] (Shinto ritual officials) for the [[Suwa-taisha]] Upper Shrine until the early [[Meiji era]]. It is situated within the grounds of the Moriya family residence.

== History ==

* In [[1989]], the 78th head of the Moriya family, [[Moriya Sanae]], and Chino City requested the design of the museum from architect [[Terunobu Fujimori]]. Construction was completed in [[1991|Heisei 3]].<ref>Fujimori's design for the building was initially titled 'Museum of Moriya.'</ref>
* The first director was [[Kosuke Hosoda|Kisuke Hosoda]], a local historian and former principal of [[Ochiai Elementary School|Fujimi Elementary School]] in [[Fujimi, Nagano|Fujimi Town]]. He served until 1995.
* The current director is Tamura Ken.

== Collection ==

The museum holds significant historical documents, including:
* [[Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba]]
* [[Nenai Shinji Shidai Kyūki]]
* [[Gofureisho]]
Additionally, it houses letters related to famous samurai such as [[Takeda Shingen]]{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)}}, [[Takeda Nobumasa]], [[Takeda Nobunawa|Takeda Nobutsuna]], [[Murakami Yoshikiyo]], and [[Sanada Masayuki]].

== Lobby Exhibition Room ==

The lobby features a recreation of offerings for the [[Onbashira Festival]], including a deer head.

== Permanent Exhibition Room ==

The permanent exhibition showcases letters and excavated artifacts. These displays are part of rotating exhibits that change every few months. For information on current exhibits, refer to the links below.

== Architecture ==

The building, designed by architect [[Terunobu Fujimori]], is a fireproof reinforced concrete structure. It incorporates natural and local materials, including:
* [[Teppeiseki]] roofing, a traditional technique revived after 50 years
* Siding made of split cypress boards using traditional methods
* Interior elements such as straw-infused mortar and hand-blown glass
Despite its revival of lost traditions, the structure avoids simple historicism, creating a unique and rooted design.<ref name="owari">"End of Architecture / Beginning of Architecture" (INAX Publishing, 2001)</ref>

Nearby, visitors can view other works by Fujimori, including [[Takasugi-an]], [[Hikusugi-an]], and [[Flying Mud Boat]], though they are generally not open to the public.

== Grounds ==
* '''Gosakuchi Shrine''': A central site of [[Mishaguji]] worship. Its forest is a designated natural monument of Chino City.
* '''Kaidōden (Prayer Hall)''': Historically used for oral transmission of family secrets, including rituals and genealogies.
* '''Jinchōkan Kofun''': A 7th-century tumulus with a diameter of approximately 9.5m. Artifacts include wooden coffin fragments, swords, and pottery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.82bunka.or.jp/bunkazai/detail.php?no=1510&seq=0|title=Jinchōkan Kofun|website=82 Cultural Properties Foundation}}</ref>
* '''Ōhōri Suwa Family Cemetery''': A burial site for the Suwa family that later became a communal graveyard.

== Access ==
* About 40 minutes on foot (2.7 km) from [[Chino Station]] ([[East Japan Railway Company|JR East]], Chūō Main Line)
* About 12 minutes on foot (900 m) from "Kami-sha" bus stop on [[Suwa Bus Aruga-Kamisha Route]]
* About 30 minutes on foot (2.2 km) from "Suwa Interchange" bus stop on [[Chūō Expressway Bus Suwa-Okaya Line]]
